spec.name: Trend v3
spec.notes: Classic trend signal on trailing returns. Weekly rebalance.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.8, annual return 11%, maximum drawdown 20%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.83 to 1.83 (change +0.00).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.83 to 1.83. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.82 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.83); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.83 against 1.83 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 1.93 against 1.83 in research, a gap of -0.10.
The best year gives 33% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 213%; Sharpe is 6.46 in calm and -6.92 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.07, so the claimed 1.80 becomes 1.73 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.89 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.07, 95th percentile 0.51).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.83 to as low as 1.39 (as low as 1.63 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (20 days) give 24% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 23% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

verdict.opinion: Paper trading only: soft test damaging (regime_split EX-6).
